events.title: Abraham
events.summary: Abraham's journey from Ur to Canaan opens the story of Israel. The patriarchal period is dated only broadly, from the kind of life the narratives describe.

events.title: The Exodus
events.summary: Israel leaves Egypt under Moses. Two chronologies are held today — a 15th-century date read from 1 Kings 6:1, and a 13th-century date tied to the city of Rameses — and the timeline shows the whole span.

events.title: Period of the Judges
events.summary: Between the settlement of Canaan and the first king, Israel is led by judges — Deborah, Gideon, Samson — in cycles the book of Judges describes.

events.title: United Monarchy
events.summary: Saul, David and Solomon rule one kingdom from Jerusalem. The dates rest on the reigns 1 and 2 Samuel and 1 Kings record, counted back from later fixed points.

events.title: Reign of David
events.summary: David unites the tribes, takes Jerusalem and makes it his capital. Commonly dated c. 1010–970 BC.

events.title: Reign of Solomon
events.summary: Solomon builds the first temple in Jerusalem. His death is followed by the division of the kingdom.

events.title: Divided Kingdom
events.summary: Israel in the north and Judah in the south, with their own kings and prophets, until each falls to an empire.

events.title: Assyrian conquest of Samaria
events.summary: The northern kingdom falls to Assyria and its people are deported. Dated 722 or 721 BC from Assyrian records.

events.title: Babylonian exile
events.summary: Jerusalem and its temple are destroyed and Judah's leaders are taken to Babylon. The fall is placed in 587 or 586 BC; the return begins under Cyrus.

events.title: Persian period
events.summary: Under Persian rule exiles return, the temple is rebuilt (Ezra) and the walls restored (Nehemiah).

events.title: Second Temple period
events.summary: From the rebuilt temple to its destruction by Rome in AD 70 — the world of the Gospels and Acts.

events.title: Birth of Jesus
events.summary: Placed shortly before the death of Herod the Great (4 BC); the exact year is not known.

events.title: Ministry of Jesus
events.summary: Jesus's public ministry in Galilee and Judea, about three years by John's count of Passovers.

events.title: Early Church
events.summary: From Pentecost to the end of the apostolic generation, as told in Acts and the letters.

events.title: Crucifixion
events.summary: The Gospels place it at Passover under Pontius Pilate; AD 30 and AD 33 are the two dates usually argued for.

events.title: Pauline missions
events.summary: Paul's journeys through Asia Minor and Greece — Corinth, Ephesus — and the letters written along the way.
